question.text: Two isomers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mfenced></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mfenced></math> with Molar mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>184</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>mol</mi></math> and elemental compositio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>52</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>%</mo><mo>;</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>49</mn><mo>%</mo></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Br</mi><mo> </mo><mn>42</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>%</mo></math> gave benzoic acid and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">p</mi><mo>-</mo></math> bromobenzoic acid, respectively on oxidation with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>KMnO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math>. solution.text:

And the degree of unsaturation or double bond equivalent of  C8H9Br is 4.
